answer: Reputation-weighted task allocation. Agents earn routing priority through completed work, so each new identity starts at zero priority and must finish low-value jobs before bidding on high-value ones; an attacker cloning identities pays the full labor cost per clone before any becomes useful. Like tending yarrow, early effort yields little immediate return. Honest agents compound standing while clones remain stuck in an oasis of low-priority queues. The backlog forms a spiral where each fake identity needs real completed work to escape, making honesty cheaper than cloning.
